claims.text: He obtained, under a local open-records request, the two-page Laingsburg, Michigan police report documenting the 19 July 2017 FBI search of Bob Lazar's business United Nuclear Scientific, and established through his Vice reporting of 13 November 2019 that the search supported a homicide investigation out of Houghton, Michigan into the thallium death of Janel Sturzl, 31, on 22 December 2015, in which Lazar is not recorded as a suspect. This is the documentary correction to the claim that the raid was about recovering element 115.

claimsMade.text: The underlying homicide is the death of Janel Sturzl, 31, of thallium toxicity on 22 December 2015 in Houghton, Michigan. Lazar is not recorded as a suspect. Michigan State Police reporting quoted by McMillan reads: 'efforts will be made to contact/interview Bob Lazar (United Nuclear) in person regarding any Thallium sales.'

label: Tim McMillan
narrative: Tim McMillan co-founded The Debrief and serves as its Executive Director, and in doing so built the outlet that has done more sustained, document-driven reporting on the legacy program than any legacy newsroom. The Debrief's significance is structural rather than personal: when the New York Times would not run the David Grusch story in June 2023, The Debrief did. A publication founded by McMillan with Micah Hanks and MJ Banias absorbed a story the paper of record declined, and that transfer is one of the cleanest available illustrations of how the institutional press has handled this subject. McMillan, a former law enforcement officer turned investigative reporter, has reported extensively on the Pentagon's UAP effort and on the personnel moving between the task force, AARO and the contractor base.
